words.en: a polite way to ask someone for help
words.note: "Could" is more polite than "can". Use it with people you do not know.

words.en: a very polite way to ask someone to do something
words.note: After "mind" use the -ing form: Would you mind closing the door?

words.en: a polite way to say what you want to do
words.note: I'd = I would. Use it in shops and offices and on the phone: I'd like to pay by card.

words.en: a polite way to ask for something in a shop or café
words.note: "Could I have the bill, please?" sounds much friendlier than "Give me the bill."

words.en: an informal way to ask if you can do something
words.note: Good with friends and colleagues: Is it OK if I leave a bit early today?

words.en: a polite way to ask if you can do something
words.note: Answer "No, not at all." if it is OK. Here "no" means yes!

words.en: a way to suggest doing something together
words.note: Use the verb without "to": Let's go to the cinema.

words.en: a friendly way to make a suggestion
words.note: "Why don't we meet at six?" is a suggestion and not a real question.

words.en: a way to suggest something
words.note: Use a noun or the -ing form: How about a coffee? How about going for a walk?

words.en: a way to suggest something or to offer to do something
words.note: Mostly used in questions with "I" and "we": Shall we take a taxi? Shall I help you?

words.en: a way to say yes to a suggestion
words.note: Shorter: Good idea! or Sounds good!

words.en: a polite way to say no to an invitation or a request

words.en: a friendly way to say no now but yes later
words.note: Say it after you say no to an invitation: Sorry, I'm busy tonight. Maybe another time.

words.en: a way to ask if someone has time on a certain day
words.note: Are you free on Thursday evening? Answer: Yes, I am. or No, sorry. I'm busy.

words.en: a polite way to ask which time is good for someone
words.note: Here "suit" means "be good for". You can also ask: When is good for you?

words.lemma: I'd like to make an appointment.
words.en: what you say when you want to book a time with a doctor or an office
words.note: We "make" an appointment. Not: do an appointment.

words.en: a way to ask for a different time
words.note: You can also say: Can we move the appointment to Friday?

words.lemma: I need to cancel my appointment.
words.en: what you say when you cannot come at the time you booked
words.note: Call as early as you can. Some places charge a fee if you cancel late.

words.en: a friendly way to say goodbye when you will meet again on a certain day
words.note: See you on Monday! Without a day: See you soon!

words.en: what you say when you arrive late
words.note: Give a short reason: Sorry I'm late. The bus was delayed.

words.lemma: Could you say that again, please?
words.en: a polite way to ask someone to repeat something
words.note: Shorter: Sorry? or Pardon? with your voice going up at the end.

words.lemma: Could you speak more slowly, please?
words.en: a polite way to ask someone to talk more slowly
words.note: Very useful on the phone. Most people are happy to help.

words.en: a way to ask someone to explain what they said
words.note: Say it in a friendly voice. With a hard voice it can sound rude.

words.en: a way to thank someone for helping you
words.note: Also: Thanks a lot! or Thank you so much!

words.en: a friendly answer when someone thanks you or says sorry
words.note: Also: You're welcome. or Don't worry about it.
